description: Belgian calibration and validation schema groundwork, by reference only. Values and source projections would resolve from Chronicle consumer facts at build time, but the current Chronicle Belgian catalog does not satisfy this full selector and period surface. Criticality tiers, relative tolerances, and target_role are validated declaration metadata only: this package does not yet wire them into runtime calibration objectives or release gates. Multi-cell series remain non-executable until Chronicle fanout produces cell-pinned references. The GRAPA row is a validation-only declaration whose Microcosm population input and PolicyEngine behavior/input support are absent. Child-benefit administrative caseload facts remain outside this target surface because the current typed target geography cannot represent their publisher-defined statistical scope or a documented scheme-to-population mapping; no child-benefit calibration or validation reference is active. The package neither constructs a national child-benefit sum nor declares behavioral take-up concepts in Axiom. No external-oracle implementation from #264 is included. The file never copies a target value from Chronicle, a survey publication, or a validation oracle.

target_references.name: statbel_population_by_age_sex_region

metadata.series: Structure of the population: age band by sex by region

target_references.notes: Non-executable series placeholder for an age-band x sex x NUTS1 count surface. Chronicle must fan this into dimension- and geography-pinned scalar references before compilation. The selector uses the typed NUTS1-2025 authority alias; a differently-vintaged source requires an explicit Chronicle projection/crosswalk. An observation for another year may enter only as a Chronicle source_projection whose fact period is the declared 2023 reference year.

target_references.name: statbel_fiscal_income_by_commune

metadata.series: Fiscal statistics of income: total net taxable income by municipality

target_references.notes: Non-executable series placeholder for commune fiscal-income cells; Chronicle must fan it into one commune-pinned scalar reference per selected cell before compilation. The eventual open commune series is diagnostic until the synthetic spine demonstrates adequate support. The selector binds the typed nis_2025 alias to the spine's 2025 NIS code set, and another code set must be projected and crosswalked in Chronicle rather than partially joined.

target_references.name: spf_finances_pit_total
target_references.notes: National assessed PIT is compared with the Axiom-computed federal and local liability on the 2022 income-year basis. Assessment-year facts must identify the represented income year in Chronicle; a period mismatch is a projection, never a silent relabeling.

target_references.name: onss_employee_contribution_total
target_references.notes: Worker-side contributions on the encoded slice. Employer-side and capped-regime totals can enter as distinct references when both the engine concepts and Ledger selectors exist.

target_references.name: onem_unemployment_caseload
target_references.notes: The initial caseload family declares the calendar-year recipient count, not a behavioral take-up rate. It remains non-executable because PolicyEngine-owned unemployment receipt/behavior input support and an exact period mapping are absent; no Axiom take-up, propensity, elasticity, or latent-draw concept is declared or implied. Pension caseload references can join this family when their Chronicle packages and distinct model mappings land. Child-benefit administrative caseload facts additionally require a typed scheme statistical scope and a documented scheme-to-population mapping.

target_references.name: sfpd_grapa_regular_payment_beneficiaries_2025_01

metadata.series: GRAPA beneficiaries in the January 2025 regular-payment population

target_references.notes: Validation-only declaration for the SFPD January 2025 regular-payment population. This is a point-in-time payment-recipient snapshot, not an eligibility denominator, annual caseload, transaction count, or behavioral take-up rate; an unresolved same-date PensionStat total also makes it unsuitable as a silent release-blocking target. PolicyEngine must own and supply a distinct receipt/behavior input before Microcosm can estimate this row. A positive Axiom entitlement or payment amount is not an observed receipt flag, and no Axiom take-up, propensity, elasticity, or latent-draw concept is declared or implied.

target_references.name: nbb_household_disposable_income
target_references.notes: Validation-tier level anchor only. The macro-realism gate may use it as a broad band, but neither the exact NBB level nor any survey- or EUROMOD-derived quantity enters the calibration objective.

demography_release.description: Population-structure cells: plus or minus 2 percent.

core_fiscal_release.description: Core fiscal totals, including assessed PIT: plus or minus 5 percent.

standard_admin_release.description: Administrative contribution totals: plus or minus 10 percent.

caseload_release.description: Administrative caseload totals: plus or minus 15 percent.

commune_diagnostic.description: Commune fiscal-income cells: plus or minus 10 percent, reported but not release-blocking.

validation_only.description: Validation oracle only; no calibration tolerance.

population_reference_2023.description: Population stock in the BE-SILC 2023 survey year.

assessment_income_year_2022.description: BE-SILC survey year 2023 carries 2022 incomes; assessed fiscal facts bind by represented income year.

calendar_year_2022.description: Calendar-year administrative or national-accounts fact aligned to the 2022 income reference year.

grapa_regular_payment_snapshot_2025_01.description: SFPD regular-payment beneficiary population observed for January 2025; no annual or behavioral take-up interpretation.
